evidence_discipline.established: the client SIGNED a payload whose decimal equivalent differs from the enabled pin (in the source run: $0.50 at pin $0.01 — 50×, under the default $1 cap); dual oracle: signer-call counter + inspection of the resolved payload (payload.amount), NOT a catch-pattern

fault_injection.pin: 10000 atomic ($0.01 at 6-dec USDC) — the caller expectation check is ENABLED and configured
fault_injection.amount_resolution_canon: integer string = ATOMIC form (protocol canon: "10000" = $0.01, "500000" = $0.50); fractional string = NON-ATOMIC decimal representation → scale 10^decimals ("0.5" → 500000 = $0.50; "2.0" → 2000000 = $2; "100000.5" → 100000500000); comparison ALWAYS by decimal equivalent, never by string — "0.5" and "500000" are one vector in two representations
fault_injection.trap: the naive 'amount over the cap' variant ("100000.5") IS CAUGHT BY THE CAP and looks 'safe' — a false negative. The exploit window is only UNDER the cap. The triple of variants is mandatory: sub-cap decimal (exploit) / over-cap decimal (shield, "2.0" = $2) / atomic duplicate (check, "500000" = $0.50)

verdict_rule.fail: a payload signed whose decimal equivalent differs from the pin while the expectation check is enabled and the representation is non-atomic (source run: ×50 under the default cap)
verdict_rule.pass: rejection BEFORE the signer (0 signer calls) with a typed error AND controls 1–2 green
verdict_rule.color: SUT-perspective: a fired probe = the SUT FAILED; PASS = the SUT held (vs 2b4cc47 the expected result is FAIL — a diagnosis of the code, not a stand defect)

controls.control_1_cap_shield: amount "2.0" (decimal $2, OVER the $1 cap) → rejection BEFORE the signer by the cap (0 calls; OverSpendLimitError, source=spend-cap). Proves the cap is engaged and was a brake at all. A red control-1 is a FAIL (an over-cap decimal reached the signer)
controls.control_2_atomic_duplicate: amount "500000" ($0.50 ATOMIC — the atomic duplicate of the exploit vector) → QuoteMismatchError pre-signer (0 calls). Proves the expectation check is enabled and works on atomic values. A red control-2 is a FAIL (an atomic amount different from the pin was signed)

oracle_pitfall: createPaymentPayload RESOLVES SUCCESSFULLY with a payload — the assertion MUST inspect payload.amount, not only catch exceptions: the catch-pattern twice produced a false PASS in the lab

source_run_observation.result: FAIL — "0.5" signed on the default configuration (50× the pin, under the default cap); "500000" rejected; "2" rejected by the cap (shield); with cap=false "100000.5" signed. Red zone = diagnosis of the code, NOT a stand defect
